_comment: Art asset registry. Single source of truth for the generation pipeline. See ../guidelines/art-pipeline.md. Every asset is declared here BEFORE it is drawn; status walks slot -> inbox -> art.

world-prop.note: Top-down orthographic. Drawn in the world at `world` px (camera is 1:1). Baked at 4x display like boat parts.

terrain.note: Reserved. Islands/shore are procedural today (bakeIslandSprite); this profile exists so the rework has a home.

illustration.note: Venue cards. Bottom fifth stays simple for the name scrim.

portrait.note: Bust crop, centered for circular use, face within central 70%.

ui-icon.note: Test over both the navy shell and bright water.

element.note: Source element for compose.py. NEVER ships on its own — a single penguin is 4-7px at race scale. Lives in art/elements/, not assets/images/.

roles.hazard: Collides or penalizes. Must telegraph before contact and hold the 3:1 contrast floor on Pearl Lagoon AND Glacier Sound.
roles.ambient: Decorative, no collision. MUST NOT be confusable with a hazard at race scale — different silhouette family, not just different color.
roles.landmark: Venue identity, on land or fixed. Never affects play.
roles.traffic: Non-racing boats. MUST NOT be confusable with a competitor at race scale (extends race-view.md 10.2).
roles.nav: Navigation aids the player is meant to read — channel markers, beacons. Canonical buoyage color coding.

anchors.center: Rotation and placement origin at the art's centroid. Floating things.
anchors.waterline: Origin where the object meets the water. Things that stick up out of it.
anchors.trunk-base: Origin at the base of the stem. Trees, reeds.
anchors.footprint: Origin at the center of the ground contact polygon. Buildings, standing birds.

assets.subject: alligator cruising just under the surface — armored ridged back and tail in olive, snout breaking the water, faint wake V behind, naturalistic not cartoon-eyed
great blue heron standing in shallows seen from above — slate wings folded, long neck tucked into an S, thin legs and their shadow in the shallow water
stilt fishing shack from above — rust corrugated roof with a simple ridge line, small dock finger reaching into the water, one moored skiff, weathered board walkway
flat-bottomed pirogue skiff from directly above — plain wooden hull, no sail and no mast, two thwarts and a push pole lying inside, unmistakably not a racing sailboat
green square day beacon on a single piling — flat square board facing up-channel, weathered post, small ring ripple at the waterline

adult orca cruising just beneath the surface seen from directly overhead — long torpedo body, broad pectoral fins swept slightly back, wide notched tail flukes, and the dorsal fin foreshortened to a short dark blade at the shoulders. This is the BACK of the animal, never the belly: the body is true black — black is one of this venue's two declared accents, so do not shift it toward navy, steel blue or charcoal — built from flat hard-edged facets, with absolutely no rim light, no outer glow or halo, and no glossy specular highlights. The black back carries exactly three pale markings and no others: a large pale grey saddle patch immediately behind the dorsal fin spanning most of the width of the back, a crisp white oval eye patch on each side near the snout, and a narrow white flash where the tail stock joins the flukes. No white on the mid-body or flanks — a broad white area there would read as an upside-down whale. Naturalistically proportioned marine mammal, never a cartoon-eyed mascot, no visible eye highlight
assets.note: Regenerated after the palette fix: dark-region blue cast dropped from +37 to +11, and the grey saddle patch — specified from the start but absent in every earlier generation — finally appeared.

This is the BACK of the animal, never the belly: true black body, crisp white oval eye patch on each side near the snout, dorsal fin foreshortened to a short dark blade at the shoulders, broad pectoral fins swept slightly back, wide notched tail flukes. assets.subject: adult orca breaking the surface, seen from directly overhead — the same individual and same construction as the cruising adult, but risen so the back sits proudly above the waterline: the black is lighter and cleaner where it is out of the water rather than seen through it, the dorsal fin reads as a distinctly taller dark blade, and a small crisp ring of white foam breaks around the shoulders where the body parts the surface. Crisp white oval eye patches, pale grey saddle patch behind the dorsal. Keep the foam tight to the body as chunky flat white shapes — no spray plume, no wake trail, no surrounding water. No rim light, no glow, no glossy speculars
assets.note: DERIVED, not prompted: edit art/masters/arctic/orca.png. USE THE CURRENT FILE — the orca family was regenerated after the palette fix and is now black (+11 blue cast) rather than navy (+37). Deriving from an older copy would give a surfacing orca that does not match its own pod. Keep the source framing and scale exactly so the two sprites are in register, or swapping poses will make the animal jump. Re-check anchorPx after ingest: the risen pose changes the silhouette. Foam is the animal's own disturbance, a deliberate exception to the class rule against baked water — keep it hugging the body.

assets.subject: orca calf cruising just beneath the surface seen from directly overhead — same construction as the adult at smaller scale, rounder blunter body, proportionally shorter dorsal fin, softer white eye patch. assets.note: Regenerated after the palette fix (art-pipeline.md 3c). Not perceptible at 50px beside them, so accepted rather than regenerated — but if the family is ever reworked, match the calf to the adults.

assets.subject: SEVEN EMPEROR penguins crowded together on ice, seen from directly overhead. COMPOSITION IS THE HARD PART — read this first: the group must look like real animals standing around at random, photographed from a drone. Arrange them IRREGULARLY and ASYMMETRICALLY. Absolutely NOT in a circle, ring, radial pattern, rosette, mandala or snowflake, and NOT evenly spaced. The centre of the group must be its DENSEST part, never an empty hole. Some birds should stand closer together than others, a couple should slightly overlap or touch, one or two should sit a little apart from the main mass, and the whole cluster should be lopsided rather than balanced. Headings should be scattered and unrelated to each bird's position — not all turned inward, not all turned outward. Keep the group compact so it fills a roughly circular-but-lumpy footprint. EACH BIRD: a compact teardrop seen from above — a glossy black back and head filling most of the shape, a short beak pointing outward, two dark flippers held slightly away from the body, a sliver of white breast at the front edge, and a vivid orange-yellow ear-and-neck flash. Seven warm yellow flecks scattered through a dark irregular mass is what identifies this species at distance, so keep every flash legible and larger than life. Keep visible dark gaps between most neighbours so the group reads as several distinct animals. Each bird is only about 12 pixels at final size, so give each a clean silhouette, its yellow flash, and nothing else. No ice, no ground, no shadow
assets.note: COMPOSED by compose.py from arctic-penguin-emperor. Two generated huddles came back as rosettes; a PRNG does irregular scatter that a diffusion model will not. Upsized ~50% over strict scale: measured, birds do not resolve below ~70px for a seven-bird group.

assets.subject: a Weddell seal hauled out and resting, seen from directly overhead — a plump elongated torpedo body tapering to paired rear flippers, a small distinctly rounded head set off from the shoulders, and two short fore-flippers held out from the sides. Mottled silver-grey and charcoal in flat hard-edged facets, with a paler belly tone showing along the flanks. CRITICAL: it must read unmistakably as a living animal and never as a rock or a chunk of ice — the head, the neck taper and the fore-flippers are what separate it from a boulder, so keep all three clearly articulated and never let the outline collapse into a plain oval. Naturalistically proportioned, never a cartoon-eyed mascot. No ice, no ground, no shadow
assets.note: Hauled out on ice, so it is judged against a PALE floe, not dark water — an ice-dwelling prop must be DARK. The OpenAI candidate was rejected for being pale mottled grey, which vanished on ISLAND_STYLES.ice. Gemini won on silhouette too: with colour removed its fore- and rear flippers still read as a four-limbed animal, where the OpenAI outline was a smooth oval indistinguishable from a rock or a penguin. Upsized ~1.5x (worldTrue 28).

assets.subject: FOUR ADELIE penguins walking in single file on ice, seen from directly overhead. DIRECTION IS CRITICAL: the line of travel runs VERTICALLY up the frame — the last bird near the bottom edge, the leader near the top edge, the others evenly between them on a gently curving track that never departs far from vertical. Every bird faces ALONG the line, i.e. toward the TOP of the frame. Do NOT run the line diagonally or across the frame; the engine rotates this sprite and treats straight up as the direction of travel. VIEWPOINT: from directly above you see the back of each bird's head and its back — no eyes, no face, no chest, with the beak foreshortened and pointing away up the frame. EACH BIRD: a compact teardrop — glossy black back and head filling most of the shape, dark flippers held slightly away from the body, a sliver of white breast at the leading edge only. SPECIES SIGNATURE: Adelies are the PLAIN penguin — solid black head with no yellow anywhere, just a fine white eye ring and a small dull pinkish beak. The absence of warm colour is the identifier; do not add any. Keep spacing close to even but not mechanical, with one bird lagging slightly, and keep every bird clearly separated. Each bird is only about 12 pixels at final size. No ice, no ground, no shadow
assets.note: COMPOSED. Vertical track, so sprite-up is the direction of travel. Upsized ~50% over strict scale: measured, birds do not resolve below ~70px for a seven-bird group.

assets.subject: ONE SINGLE emperor penguin standing on ice, seen from directly overhead, centred and filling the frame, facing the TOP of the frame. assets.subject: ONE SINGLE GENTOO penguin standing on ice, seen from directly overhead. A compact teardrop: the body is TRUE NEUTRAL BLACK — not blue-black, not navy, not steel blue, not charcoal. This bird sits in a blue venue and the model's instinct will be to tint it to match; do not. Hold the blacks neutral and the overall colour nearly desaturated, with only the species marking carrying saturated colour. The back and the back of the head fill most of the shape, two dark flippers held slightly out from the body, and a sliver of white breast at the leading edge only. TWO SPECIES SIGNATURES, both of which an overhead camera sees well and both of which must be unmistakable. FIRST, colour: a bold white BONNET patch sits across the top of the crown, running side to side over the eyes like a headband, paired with a bright orange-red beak foreshortened and pointing away up the frame. SECOND, silhouette: gentoos have a long stiff wedge-shaped TAIL that projects clearly behind the body, so the teardrop ends in a distinct pointed tail spur rather than a smooth curve — this is the one penguin whose outline is not a plain teardrop. Crisp flat faceted shading, a clean dark contour no heavier than the rest of the set, no glossy speculars, no white halo behind the bird. Exactly one bird, alone. No ice, no ground, no shadow
assets.note: The only penguin with TWO overhead-readable identifiers: a white crown bonnet (colour, on top of the head) and a projecting stiff tail (silhouette). Element; composed into groups, never ships alone. Colour wording corrected: the macaroni and gentoo subjects had asked for 'blue-black', and emperor/adelie only described black passively. A passive colour description loses to the model's prior in a blue venue; the orca reached +11 blue-cast only once its subject actively refused navy. All four now carry that refusal.

assets.subject: a temperate tidal estuary at low water, aerial-oblique, horizon just below the top quarter. THE SAND IS THE DOMINANT COLOR: broad exposed sandbars filling roughly half the picture in confident warm amber-gold, built from bold chunky faceted planes, dry crowns bright and sunlit, wet margins a much darker ochre where the tide has just left, crisp scalloped edges, bold branching drain-runnels cut into them. ONE sinuous channel of DEEP SATURATED SLATE-BLUE water — a rich blue-grey with real blue in it, never neutral grey — winds from the plain empty foreground back toward a distant sea, and it is the eye-path: big angular ripple planes in two clear tones, carrying bright white current streaks and eddy curls that show which way the water is running. A line of leaning rust-red withy markers, bundled sticks, steps irregularly along the channel edge into the distance. The focal element is a small loose group of FOUR SPOON-BILLED SANDPIPERS on the nearest bar — plump little shorebirds with the distinctive flat spatulate spoon-shaped bill tip, warm brown backs and white bellies, bold simplified two-tone shapes rather than feather-by-feather naturalism, one with wings raised, the others feeding head-down. SKY WITH REAL VARIETY: several big rounded blob-stack cumulus of clearly DIFFERENT sizes, each with a single flat shade tone underneath, at different heights, mixed with a few thin horizontal streak clouds — not a uniform band of identical wisps. Green is limited to one thin dark shore line at the horizon and nowhere else. STRICTLY EXCLUDE: neutral grey or desaturated water; muted, washed-out or pastel color; naturalistic wildlife-illustration rendering; long down-curved curlew bills; turquoise or tropical water; flamingos or any pink bird; otters or any mammal; broad green marsh grass; evenly repeated identical clouds; any grass, bird or object in the lower fifth of the frame
assets.note: Regen 4. Pass 1 drifted tropical (marsh/flamingos/otter). Pass 2 specced pewter-pastel, measured 0.185 sat vs set 0.66-0.94 and read unfinished. Pass 3 gold-dominant fixed that but water stayed neutral grey (0.507). Pass 4 cut to 4 large birds; with blue water it reaches 0.693 = in range. This pass: deeper slate blue, varied cumulus, and the spoon-billed sandpipers PINNED BY NAME so they survive regeneration (Wes liked them; the spatulate bill is the charm).

assets.subject: ONE wandering albatross in flight, soaring, seen from directly overhead — enormous slender wings held straight out and locked, not flapping, spanning nearly the full width of the frame and giving the bird a long thin CROSS silhouette unlike anything else. Body and back are white, the upperwing surfaces darken toward the trailing edge and finish in clean black wingtips, and the short wedge tail trails behind. The heavy pale hooked bill leads, pointing to the TOP of the frame. Wings are narrow and stiff with a subtle backward sweep, never broad or rounded. Crisp flat faceted shading, a clean dark contour no heavier than the rest of the set, no glossy speculars, no motion blur. Exactly one bird, alone. No water, no ground, NO SHADOW — the engine draws the shadow that makes it read as airborne
assets.note: AIR-LAYER PROP. Needs two engine pieces that do not exist yet: a draw pass above the boats, and a displaced shadow on the water. The shadow IS the altitude cue — without it a bird seen from directly overhead reads as floating, not flying. `world` folds in three things: true wingspan at 9.2px/m, the ~1.5x recognition exaggeration, and an altitude magnification (a bird at height is closer to the camera, so it is genuinely larger — not a cheat). Sprite carries NO shadow. Solitary by nature, so one bird alone is correct rather than a compromise.

assets.subject: ONE snow petrel in flight, seen from directly overhead, centred and filling the frame, flying toward the TOP. Wings spread and slightly swept back in a shallow M, short wedge tail behind, small head leading. The snow petrel is UNIFORMLY WHITE — body, back, and both wings from shoulder to wingtip, with no dark wingtips, no dark trailing edge and no grey banding. Think of a white dove rather than a gull or an albatross. The only non-white parts are a small black bill and a black eye. Shade the white with the faintest cool grey planes only, just enough to show the wing surfaces turning, and give it a clean thin dark contour so the shape still separates when it passes over pale ice. Crisp flat faceted shading, no glossy speculars, no motion blur. Exactly one bird, alone. No water, no ground, NO SHADOW

Root cause was the prompt's own palette clause, which told every arctic prop to commit to steel navy; that clause is now context-only for props. Its unbroken whiteness is why this asset exists: the only bright object in the darkest venue.

assets.subject: An inflatable racing mark floating on open water, seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD — looking straight down onto it from a helicopter, with none of its side or bottom rim visible anywhere, not even at the near edge. THINK OF IT AS A LOW THREE-SIDED PYRAMID, not a flat cushion. It is a squat tetrahedron: a rounded triangular base with three big triangular faces that SLOPE UPWARD and inward to meet at a single blunt apex directly above the centre. Seen from above you are looking down at those three sloping faces, and the three ridges where they meet run from the central apex out to the three rounded corners, forming a clean three-spoke Y. A bold dark lifting ring sits on the apex at the centre — make it a solid, chunky ring, not a hairline, because it is the one focal dot. THREE FACES, THREE CLEARLY DIFFERENT VALUES — this is the hardest requirement and the whole point of the pyramid form. Because each face tilts in a different direction, each catches the single light source differently. Render them as roughly 100%, 75% and 50% brightness: one face bright, one clearly mid, one clearly dark, with a hard crisp edge along every ridge. The engine desaturates inactive marks to flat slate grey for most of the race, so hue differences are worthless — CONVERTED TO GREYSCALE the three faces, the Y-ridge and the centre ring must all still read instantly. A mark that is one even tone with faint seams is a failure. COLOUR: true safety orange, warm and mid-bright, not red and not scarlet. Flat poster-like colour within each face — absolutely no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight, no smooth gradient, no plastic sheen. A narrow band of deeper wetter orange runs around the very bottom edge where the fabric meets the water. ROTATION: placed at an arbitrary angle with no 'up' — the three faces, ridges and corners must be identical in size and shape so the three-fold symmetry looks deliberate however it is turned, and the apex must sit at the exact centre of the frame. Drawn at only about 30 pixels: bold simple silhouette, a thin clean contour no heavier than the rest of the set, no detail that would not survive that size. No numbers, no letters, no flag, no water, no ripple, no shadow
assets.note: Venue-agnostic: the only prop on all ten venues, so no venue palette clause. Replaces the 160x140 oblique mark.png with a 2048 square master. ENGINE FACTS: drawMarkBodies() draws it at W=30 and applies an arbitrary per-mark rotation, so the art has no 'up' and three-fold symmetry is correct here — the opposite of the group-prop rule against symmetry (hence allowSymmetry). THE INACTIVE-STATE TEST WAS UNWINNABLE AND TWO CANDIDATES WERE REJECTED FOR FAILING IT. getMarkImgGray() tints inactive marks with source-atop rgba(148,163,184,0.8), i.e. 0.2*art + 0.8*slate, so exactly 20% of any value difference survives BY CONSTRUCTION. Measured three-face value spread, active -> inactive: incumbent 54.4 -> 10.9, candidate A 39.7 -> 7.9, this one 28.8 -> 5.8. At 30px all three are the same grey triangle when inactive. Inactive legibility is a CODE parameter, not an art problem: dropping the tint from 0.8 to ~0.55 recovers 45% instead of 20% and visibly helps whatever art is used. SHIPPED: the higher-contrast candidate, chosen by eye. It also measured best of the two new ones on three-face value spread (39.7 active / 7.9 inactive, against the alternative's 28.8 / 5.8), so the preference matched the metric. Its known deviation is colour: body RGB (202,57,9) reads scarlet rather than the safety orange the subject asked for — the incumbent sat at (225,108,44). Left as-is because the extra saturation is part of why it reads at 30px, but if the mark ever looks too red against the warm venues (redrock, swamp), that is the number to change. Upsized 30 -> 60 on 2026-07-28 at the request of the designer: the top-down form has less visual mass than the old oblique one, which cheated the projection to show its sides. NOTE the collision radius (markRadius = 12 in script.js, so 24 units across) was deliberately NOT changed — the visible mark is now 2.5x the collider. That is forgiving rather than punishing, but boats will visibly overlap the mark without penalty. Changing markRadius would alter physics and invalidate the eval baseline.

scale.anchor: The player's boat. Hull is ~56 world units (see the repositionBoats comment in script.js) and the camera is 1:1, so 56px = one boat.
scale.boatLength: Treat the boat as a ~20ft (6.1m) sportboat. Nothing in the game names a class, so this is a free choice — and it is the one that makes the accepted art self-consistent. At J/105 scale (10.5m) everything already accepted would be ~2x oversize.
scale.note: Exaggeration is permitted and often required: a penguin's true overhead footprint is ~0.5m = 4.6px, which cannot carry a silhouette. Measured on arctic water, a 7-bird huddle needs ~70px before individual birds resolve and species colour appears. Exaggerate deliberately and record it here; do not drift.
